name: Premvati Food Court at Akshardham
why_it_matters: The food court inside Swaminarayan Akshardham temple complex — runs on satvik principles (pure-veg, no onion, no garlic, no eggs). Caters to 8,000+ daily visitors during Akshardham peak. The khichdi-kadhi is the order most pilgrims come back for; multi-cuisine layout (North, South, Chinese, fast food) all in the same Swaminarayan dietary restriction. Cleanest food-court hygiene in Gandhinagar.
insider_tip: Akshardham (and Premvati) is closed on Mondays and the temple closes at 7pm — plan around that. Avoid the 1-2pm lunch rush. Khichdi-kadhi is the signature; everything else is good-for-a-food-court but unremarkable. No cash-card at counters; the temple uses a prepaid card system.
signature_address: Inside Swaminarayan Akshardham, Sector 20, J Road, Gandhinagar, Gujarat 382020

name: Hotel Cambay Sapphire Multi-Cuisine Restaurant
why_it_matters: 28-acre 4-star resort on GIDC Sector 25 — 199 rooms, golf course on site, multi-cuisine restaurant with pool-side seating. The Sunday brunch buffet is the city's reference brunch destination for state-government and Mahatma Mandir / business-traveller crowds. Wins where Premvati doesn't (alcohol-free is still the city default but Cambay caters to corporate guests).
insider_tip: Sunday brunch (11am-3pm) is the value play — buffet covers brunch and lunch, kitchen runs sharpest. Reservations required for weekend dinner. Skip the European section; the tandoor and Indian counters are stronger. Pool-side dinner in winter is the best seat in the house.
signature_address: Hotel Cambay Sapphire, Plot 22-24, GIDC, Sector 25, Gandhinagar, Gujarat 382044

name: Havmor Ice Cream
signature_dish: Sundae and seasonal kesar ice cream
why_it_matters: Founded 1944 in Karachi by Satish Chona, moved to Ahmedabad after Partition — 81-year-old Gujarat-grown ice cream chain, now under LOTTE Wellfood. The Sector 11 Gandhinagar outlet is the city's reference ice cream parlour. Alphonso mango ice cream in summer is the seasonal must-buy; the brand pioneered the Indian-flavour-on-vanilla-base template most local brands now copy.
insider_tip: Summer (Mar-Jun) is the mango ice cream window — order the alphonso variant, not the generic mango. Kesar pista kulfi is the year-round must-buy. Avoid the sundae section if you want value; the single-scoop with toppings is the better-priced order.
signature_address: Shop 6-7, President Tower, Near CH 3 Circle, Sector 11, Gandhinagar, Gujarat 382010

name: Sankalp Restaurant
why_it_matters: Sankalp is the Gujarat-grown South Indian chain — Sector 16 Gandhinagar outlet is the default 'south indian here?' answer in the planned-city sector layout. Dosa-uttapam-idli served at a price point that pulls government-employee lunch crowds and student groups from Gujarat National Law University.
insider_tip: Lunch (12-3pm) gets the freshest batter. The mysore masala dosa is the second-most-ordered dish — slightly spicier than the standard masala. Skip the Indo-Chinese section; the kitchen is calibrated for South Indian only.

name: Mary Gold Restaurant
why_it_matters: Sector 16 is Gandhinagar's central restaurant cluster (opposite GH 5 government building); Mary Gold is one of the trusted multi-cuisine anchors there. State-government office lunches drive 60%+ of weekday traffic. The Gujarati thali is competently done, not exceptional; the value is the working-day convenience and the parking.
insider_tip: Weekday lunch (1-2:30pm) is the rush — go before or after. The Gujarati thali is the order if you only have one meal here; the multi-cuisine sections are good-not-great. Skip on Sundays — half the city's open eateries are closed and Mary Gold's quality drops with the rush.
